reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address FeMnNiGeSi alloys, nanoscale thin films, or the specific mechanisms of strain and compositional inhomogeneity. E1 mentions a reduced magnetocaloric effect in nanocrystalline samples of a different material, and E2 discusses refrigerant capacity in bulk HEAs without hysteresis, providing no support for the key premises.
premises: Nanoscale interfacial strain and compositional inhomogeneities pin magnetic domain walls in FeMnNiGeSi films.
These features disrupt the cooperative magnetostructural transition, reducing the magnetic entropy change peak and increasing hysteresis.
Post-deposition annealing relieves interfacial strain and reduces compositional inhomogeneities.
Relaxation of strain promotes more uniform magnetic ordering and sharpens the magnetocaloric effect.
The broadened transition and hysteresis in as-deposited films are due to low-dimensional processing.
